outputs.headline: False: Drinking hot water with lemon juice does not kill coronavirus
outputs.summary: There is no scientific proof that hot water with lemon juice cures, kills, or protects against the coronavirus.
outputs.what_post_claims: The post claims that drinking hot water mixed with lemon juice kills the coronavirus.
outputs.what_is_true: Medical experts and global health agencies state that drinking hot water with lemon juice does not cure or kill the coronavirus inside the body.
evidence_against: The World Health Organization confirmed there is no scientific evidence that lemon drinks or warm water prevent or cure coronavirus.
Medical specialists reported through FactCheck.org that acidic juices or hot beverages do not kill the virus in the human body.
Health advisories from AFP Fact Check and Snopes found no proof that home lemon remedies protect against the infection.
outputs.sources_spoken: the World Health Organization and FactCheck.org
outputs.audio_script: A viral post claims that drinking hot water mixed with lemon juice kills the coronavirus. This claim is false. Medical experts explain that while lemon water is a normal, refreshing drink, it has no power to destroy the virus in your body or protect you from infection. There is simply no scientific evidence behind this home remedy. We are very sure about this conclusion. It is based on clear medical advice and findings from the World Health Organization and FactCheck.org.
card_lines: Claim: Hot water with lemon juice kills coronavirus
Truth: It does not kill, cure, or prevent the virus
